value.body: A textile process engineer runs the wet-processing stages — pre-treatment, dyeing, printing and finishing — that turn grey fabric or yarn into finished material. Processing houses, composite mills and garment exporters with their own dye houses hire them. A day involves planning batches, checking shades and test results, and solving problems on the floor.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech Textile Chemistry or Textile Technology

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Dyeing machines, colour-matching systems, test lab equipment

items.label: Work pattern
items.value: Shift duty on the processing floor is common

items.label: Direct employment in textiles
items.note: Whole sector, from fibre to garments; an estimate, not a yearly count

items.label: Textiles & apparel share of India's exports

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join a processing house or composite mill as a trainee in the dyeing or finishing department, through campus placement or direct application.

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: dyeing master, processing manager, technical service for dye and chemical firms.
Effluent rules shape how plants operate, so environmental compliance is part of the job.
Work is plant-based, mostly in textile clusters.
